blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Field errors are conveyed by colour alone, with no text and no programmatic state) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: Fails WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. A screen reader user who tabs out of the postcode field with `ABC` hears nothing: the border change is not announced and the field is not exposed as invalid, so they reach submit without knowing what is wrong; a colour-blind user cannot tell a red border from the grey one. Add a text message under each invalid field, associated with `aria-describedby`, set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input, and keep the red border as a secondary cue (optionally with an icon). The rejected alternative ("a message under each field") is the one the criterion requires. Carry it into the spec — the scenarios "An invalid postcode" and "A corrected field" only assert the border colour ("the field's border turns red", "the border returns to grey") and should assert the message text and its association — and into task 1.2.
findings.title: Field errors are conveyed by colour alone, with no text and no programmatic state

findings.evidence: - The error list at the top of the form is removed.
findings.recommendation: The plan says nothing about what happens on submit when fields are still invalid (a field never visited, or the customer pressing Enter in the form). With the top list gone and no message per field, a keyboard or screen reader user presses submit and nothing is announced and focus does not move — WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 2.4.3 Focus Order. Add a decision and a scenario: on submit with errors, validate every field, show each field's message, and move focus to the first invalid field (or keep an error summary with links to the fields, announced on submit).
findings.title: Submitting with invalid fields gives no feedback once the error list is removed
